brief:
本課程著重於環境微生物之基礎、生態與其在環境科學上的應用。微生物基礎部分包括細菌、真菌、藻類等微生物之分類、形態
和生理基本特性、培養、生長、代謝與控制等學理與操作技術等。而微生物生態則以其碳、氮循環與個別代謝的生化反應為基
礎，說明各類微生物於環境生態中所扮演的角色和重要性。同時說名類微生物之特殊生理代謝能力得於應用在能源工業、廢水和
廢棄物處理、生態環境復育，及農業等領域的學理依據與技術。
keywords: Course keywords: 微生物生態，環境微生物學，微生物指標，應用微生物學，生物環境復育

brief:
本課程以頭前溪流域為學習場域，結合永續發展目標（SDGs）、環境治理與設計思考方法，帶領學生從真實世界問題出發，探討
河川生態、水質污染、水資源治理、環境正義及地方文化等議題。課程透過課堂講授、實地走讀、專家座談、資料分析與團隊
專題等方式，培養學生跨域整合、問題分析、利害關係人溝通及社會實踐能力。學生將運用設計思考流程，發展兼顧環境、社
會與治理面向之創新方案，並藉由與在地社群、學校及公民團體互動，深化對流域治理與公共參與的理解，培養面對永續發展
挑戰所需之專業能力與社會責任。
content: Course keywords: 永續環境治理 Sustainable Environmental Governance,設計思考 Design Thinking,流域治理 Watershed Governance,水資源管理 Water Resource Management,社會實踐與公民參與 Social Practice and Civic Engagement      永續環境治理的設計思考Design Thinking for Sustainable Environmental Governance: Living in Harmony with the Hsinchu River一、課程說明（Course Description）頭前溪是孕育新竹地區發展的重要流域，也是新竹縣市民生用水、生態環境與產業發展的重要基礎。本課程以頭前溪流域為學習場域，結合永續發展目標（SDGs）、環境治理、設計思考（Design Thinking）及大學社會責任（USR）理念，引導學生從真實世界問題出發，探討河川生態、水質污染、水資源管理、環境正義、公民參與及地方文化等議題。課程透過課堂講授、跨域討論、專家座談、實地踏查、資料分析與團隊專題等方式，培養學生問題分析、利害關係人溝通、跨域整合及方案設計能力。學生將運用設計思考流程，從問題同理、需求探索、問題定義、方案發想、原型設計到成果驗證，提出兼顧環境、社會與治理面向之創新方案。本課程特別強調「從流域認識地方、從地方理解永續」，鼓勵學生走入頭前溪流域現場，透過與地方社群、學校、公民團體及政府部門互動，理解環境治理的複雜性與多元利害關係人觀點，培養未來面對永續發展挑戰所需之專業能力與社會責任感。---二、指定用書（Text Books）教師自編講義、案例教材及補充閱讀資料。---三、參考書籍（References）1. Brown, T. (2009). *Change by Design: How Design Thinking Creates New Alternatives for Business and Society.*2. United Nations. *Transforming Our World: The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.*3. United Nations World Water Development Report.4. EPA (United States Environmental Protection Agency) Water Resources and Public Participation Resources.5. Climate Change Impacts on Freshwater Resources, EPA.6. Kernan, M., Battarbee, R., & Moss, B. (2010). *Climate Change Impacts on Freshwater Ecosystems.*7. 台灣河溪網（Taiwan River Network）8. 荒野保護協會（Society of Wilderness）9. 我們要喝乾淨水行動聯盟10. 頭前溪流域相關研究報告、政府公開資料及教師指定閱讀。---#四、教學方式（Teaching Methods）本課程採取「問題導向學習（PBL）」與「場域導向學習（Place-based Learning）」方式進行。教學方式包含：1. 課堂講授（Lectures）   * 永續發展、流域治理、水資源管理及設計思考相關理論。2. 分組討論（Group Discussion）   * 問題分析、需求探索及方案發想。3. 實地踏查（Field Study）   * 頭前溪流域、水環境場域及相關設施參訪。4. 專家座談（Guest Speakers）   * 邀請學界、政府、NGO及實務工作者分享經驗。5. 專題實作（Project-based Learning）   * 學生團隊提出永續環境治理方案。6. 成果展示（Presentation）   * 期中與期末成果發表與交流。---五、教學進度（Course Schedule）Week 1　課程介紹與頭前溪流域概論Week 2-3　實地走讀：舊港島、南寮及頭前溪出海口（9/19全天）Week 4　頭前溪流域地理、水文與歷史發展Week 5　河川生態、水質污染與環境風險Week 6　專家講座：河川廢棄物與公民科學Week 7　流域實地考察與現場觀察Week 8　頭前溪與新竹城市發展Week 9　期中成果報告Week 10　永續治理案例與利害關係人參與Week 11　公私協力與水環境巡守實務Week 12　關西鳳山溪走讀Week 13　竹東流域文化與地方走讀Week 14　垃圾處理與循環經濟場域參訪Week 15　水質大數據分析與治理應用Week 16　期末成果發表與方案展示---六、成績考核（Evaluation）課堂參與與出席　　　　　20%（含課堂討論、活動參與）團隊合作與平時作業　　　30%期中專題成果　　　　　　20%期末專題成果　　　　　　30%學生請假規定依《國立清華大學學生請假辦法》辦理。本課程包含多次實地踏查及場域學習活動，若因特殊原因無法參與校外教學活動，須依學校規定完成請假程序，並於事前通知授課教師。經核准請假者，應依教師指定方式完成替代學習作業，以維護學習權益。無故缺席校外活動者，將視同缺課並影響課堂參與成績。---七、生成式AI使用規範（AI Usage Policy）■ 有條件開放（Conditionally Open）本課程鼓勵學生善用生成式AI工具（如ChatGPT、Claude、Gemini等）作為學習輔助工具，例如資料蒐集、文獻摘要、構想發想、簡報整理及文本潤飾等。惟學生須遵守以下原則：1. AI不得取代學生之獨立思考與分析。2. 專題報告與作業須明確說明AI工具使用情形。3. 學生需自行查證AI產出內容之正確性。4. 實地觀察、田野調查、數據分析與個人反思不得完全由AI代為完成。5. 教師得要求學生說明作品形成過程及AI使用方式。未依規定揭露AI使用情形者，得視情況調整成績評定。---八、課程相關網站（Course-related Website）1. 聯合國永續發展目標（SDGs）   https://sdgs.un.org/goals2. 台灣河溪網   https://www.twrna.org3. 荒野保護協會   https://www.sow.org.tw4. 我們要喝乾淨水行動聯盟   https://www.facebook.com/hsinchu.drink5. 頭前溪流域行動平台（課程期間提供）

brief:
This course is designed to provide a basic understanding of surface analysis techniques and the 
applications how surface analysis can be utilized in research. In addition to conventional 
characterization, advanced experimental design for surface analysis, such as synchrotron-based 
techniques, in situ methodologies and time-resolved experiments, are also introduced in this course.

本課程介紹質譜技術於環境分析之原理與應用，涵蓋液相與氣相層析串聯質譜（LC–MS/MS、GC–MS/MS）及感應耦合電漿質譜
（ICP–MS），並說明不同類型污染物之分析策略。課程強調環境污染物之檢測原理與應用，培養學生於環境監測與污染分析之基
本能力。
content: Course keywords: 環境質譜分析、新興污染物、層析分離技術、微量分析、環境監測 Environmental Mass Spectrometry、Emerging Contaminants、Chromatographic Separation、Trace Analysis、Environmental Monitoring      一、課程說明(Course Description)本課程旨在建立學生對質譜技術於環境分析中之核心概念與應用能力，內容涵蓋層析分離（液相與氣相液相）與質譜分析之整合，並結合LC–MS/MS、GC–MS/MS及ICP–MS等主流分析平台。課程將說明不同污染物之分析方法與儀器選擇原則，並介紹樣品前處理、定量分析、品質控制及數據判讀等關鍵技術。此外，亦將涵蓋新興污染物分析、非目標篩選及轉化產物鑑定等進階主題，修課學生將具備跨領域之環境分析能力，並能將質譜技術應用於實際研究問題。二、指定用書(Text Books)“Introduction to MassSpectrometry” J.T. Watson and O.D.Sparkman, 4th Edition, Wiley.“Mass Spectrometry-Principles andApplications” Edmond de Hoffmannand Vincent Stroobant, 3rd Edition,Wiley三、參考書籍(References)四、教學方式(Teaching Method)Lecture五、教學進度(Syllabus)LC–MS/MS、GC–MS/MS、ICP–MS六、成績考核(Evaluation)1.Midterm: 40%2.Final exam: 40%3.Report: 20%七、可連結之網頁位址

brief:
This course will introduce the detection and analysis methods, environmental occurrence/distribution, 
environmental fate and treatment technology of emerging pollutants in water environments.
content: Course keywords: Emerging Contaminants, Water Pollution, Water Reuse, Wastewater Treatment, Environmental Science and Engineering      課程說明 (Course Description)This course will introduce the detection and analysis methods, environmental occurrence/distribution, environmental fate and treatment technology of emerging pollutants in water environments. This course enables students to understand the importance of emerging contaminant issues in the field of environmental science and engineering.指定用書 (Text Books)、參考書籍 (References)與本課程相關之英文期刊論文教學方式 (Teaching Methods)投影片授課、小組討論教學進度 (Course Schedule)*course introduction/overview of environmental emerging contaminants*definition and origin of emerging contaminants*detection instruments/methods of emerging contaminants*environmental occurrence of emerging contaminants in water environments*environmental fate of emerging contaminants*Treatment technology*Risk/health issue of emerging contaminants成績考核 (Evaluation)class participation/presentation 30%midterm exam 30%final presentation/report 40%

brief:

operating principles, and explain the collection efficiency and application of various control 
equipment.

brief:
This course introduces students to the core concepts and methods of statistics, with a
focus on learning how to use data effectively in the face of uncertainty. Key topics
include data visualization, descriptive statistics, probability, statistical inference, and
linear regression. Emphasis will be placed on building intuition and practical
understanding rather than mathematical rigor.
Students will develop the skills to make sense of data, draw meaningful conclusions,
and communicate results with clarity and confidence. The tools and thinking
developed in this course are valuable for making informed decisions and conducting
research across a wide range of disciplines. They also form the foundation of many
modern applications, including machine learning and artificial intelligence.

brief:
本門課程設計從基礎的程式設計開始，透過循序漸進的修課規劃，讓學生除有完備的人工智慧技術外，也了解相關倫理議
題，最後透過人工智慧專題應用，讓學生們?972;解人工智慧技術在產業上?768;地的考?870;。因此本課程設定適合所有跨
域(非電資專業)的學生。旨在培養學生運用邏輯思維解決問題的能力，位居人類知識版圖中「計算思維」與「工具理性」的
交會處。程式設計不再只是工程師的專利，而是現代公民理解世界與參與社會的基本素養之一。從智慧型手機應用到醫療數
據分析，程式無所不在；本課程讓來自不同背景的學生能以程式語言參與這個由數位邏輯驅動的社會。透過設計演算法、撰
寫簡易應用程式，學生將不僅學會「如何寫程式」，更能體會「如何用邏輯思考」，落實人類追求真理、效率與創新之普世價
值。

brief:
金融科技(Financial Technology, FinTech)是目前全球金融業與科技業的焦點，它所引發的破壞式創新，正挑戰既有金融
服務的供給方式和消費行為。本課程由資工、數學教授群共同開設，旨在釐清 FinTech 本質、相關的創新科技、以及關鍵的趨
勢。
同時我們也會在課程當中邀請相關學者專家進行演講，並在金融機構（或金融科技新創公司）的協助之下完成期末的AI程式競
賽。歡迎想參與或是有志於跨金融與科技領域的同學們，來共同一窺金融科技殿堂之美。

brief:
In this course, Physical AI serves as the central lens through which all projects and discussions
are contextualized. Students will explore how modern AI models are integrated into real-world
systems such as robots, smart homes, and autonomous vehicles, and how intelligence,
embodiment, and environment jointly shape system behavior.
As AI systems increasingly operate around us in everyday life, critical questions emerge: How
do these systems function in real-world settings? How do we ensure their reliability, safety, and
alignment with human values? And what new challenges arise when AI is deployed in open,
dynamic environments?
If these questions inspire you, this course is designed for you.

brief:
自二十世紀初現代考古學從西方傳入中國，這門學問便很快地在歷史悠久、族群及文化多元的中國土地上生根成長，至今已取
得了大量的研究資料和豐富的研究成果，不只對促進中國古代人類文化和歷史研究及文明進程的新理解有重要的貢獻，即使對
其它人文、社會科學，甚而自然科學領域的一些研究課題，例如:中國古代的社會型態、經濟變遷、工藝美術、科技發展、宗
教禮制、民族發展、族群遺傳、農業起源和天文星象等，也提供了非常珍貴的出土資料與證據。有些考古發現甚而成為令人嚮
往的世界文化遺產。因此，過去半個多世紀以來的這段時間，考古學在中國成為一門顯學，被稱為是中國考古學的黃金時代。
	本課程的目的是要介紹中國考古學的發展、發現，以及重要的研究成果和所探討的重要課題，期使選課的同學對中
國考古學有所認識和瞭解，並培養研究的視野、興趣和發展的能力。

the ancient hunters and gathers in China

brief:

瓷器類別，尤其是貿易陶瓷的部分，並同時討論生產技術的發展與傳播、運輸航路與消費地的脈絡與再脈絡化、科學分析資料等等。
本課程為討論課，學生將專責收集特定主題的材料於課堂上發表，並藉由實際接觸庫房材料、建置檔案了解考古學觀察陶瓷器的重點。

brief:
本課程為《人類學方法論》的進階課程，主要目的在於訓練學生具有從事獨立研究之能力。所有選修過《人類學方法論》之同
學，必須在暑假期間從事一個短期的可行性田野研究，實際體驗田野調查工作，練習操作人類學之研究方法，整理及分析田野資
料，最後並將之書寫成研究成果報告，在學生之田野實習成果發表會中公開發表。期使學生經由實際之田野經驗，對人類學研究
之性質及方法有進一步地認識。最後，我們希望田野實習能做為學生將來發展其碩、博士論文的基礎。未修過《人類學方法論》
者，無法修選本門課，請留意。

brief:
This seminar examines the relationships between the indigenous peoples and the  
state in Taiwan through historical periods, situating it in the settler colonial contexts.  
Historical reflection on the changing relationship between the indigenous peoples  
and the state equipped students to explain the contemporary dilemma faced by the 
indigenous people worldwide. With the concept of transitional justice emerging in  
Taiwan and elsewhere, this seminar will draw on materials and experiences in other  
Fourth World to compare with those of Taiwan’s indigenous peoples and seek to  
advance a better path forward.
keywords: Course keywords: Historical and Transitional Justice; Settler Colonialism
Reconciliation  (歷史與轉型正義/定居殖民主義/第四世界/新自由主義/和解)
restrictions: 排除大學部1年級2年級3年級

brief:
在日常生活中，許多時候情緒與倫理幾乎無法分開，而這份交纏並不止於私人生活，在現代制度之中同樣運作。本課程便從這份交纏出發，
借助人類學中兩個重要卻長期平行發展的理論傳統來理解它：倫理轉向（ethical turn）與情緒人類學（anthropology of 
emotions）。前者問的是人們如何在日常生活中成為倫理主體，後者則把情緒當作一個可以被田野觀察與描述的問題，去看人們如何在語
言、身體與人際關係之中感受、命名並賦予情緒意義。情緒的養成與倫理主體的形成，何以在許多時候難以分開，正是這門課想要一路追問
的問題。
restrictions: 排除大學部1年級2年級3年級

brief:
本專題課程聚焦臺灣最南端的恆春半島，自約五千年前舊石器時代晚期延續型文化至金屬器時代之發展歷程，該時期不僅銜接
史前與歷史階段，更構成臺灣近代史的重要基礎場景。課程聚焦考古學文化類型討論、生態人類學與跨領域自然科學研究方
法，引導學生探索史前文化的變遷脈絡與族群互動，培養整合分析與問題探究能力。
　　在內容設計上，首先認識各時期史前考古文化之內涵，進一步深入探討史前人群如何因應多元的海陸域生態環境，發展出
漁撈、狩獵、採集與栽培作物利用的複合型生業模式。這些多樣化的適應策略，使恆春半島的史前時代出現高度多元適應型
態，從生計韌性理論（Resilience Theory in Archaeology）探討該區域在不同時期的適應模式。其次，物質文化以貝器加
工場為核心，分析其工藝技術與器物類型，說明其在南島語族臺灣起源論中的重要性，並探討其所呈現的專業分工與區域交流
現象。培養學生對臺灣史前文化的系統性認識，並建立其對人群遷徙、環境適應與文化交流之整體理解。此外透過玉石器、骨
角牙器與陶器類型的比較研究，課程將引導學生辨識臺灣東西部之間可能存在的史前交通要道，理解物質文化如何呈現文化傳
播與區域互動的線索。最後，結合體質
keywords: Course keywords: 恆春半島考古、鵝鑾鼻考古遺址群、生態適應、工藝技術、南島語族起源 Archaeology of the Hengchun Peninsula
restrictions: 排除大學部1年級2年級3年級

brief:
本課程將引導學生系統性認識考古學中石器研究的核心理論與分析方法，透過討論與案例分析，理解石器在重建人類行為與社會組織中的關
鍵角色。石器作為考古遺存中最常見且保存良好的材料之一，不僅提供了理解史前技術與日常實踐的證據，更是連結環境、經濟與文化行為
的重要媒介。課程內容涵蓋石器的類型特徵、原料選擇與取得策略、製作技術與操作序列、分類原則等基礎，以及技術組織理論、功能研
究、實驗考古學、民族考古學、過程與後過程等分析取徑，也討論如何從石器探討生計活動、勞動分工、資源利用與貿易交換等議題。透過
系統性的理論學習、案例研讀與實作訓練，學生將建立石器辨識、記錄與分析的基礎能力，也理解石器技術與使用策略所反映的人群行為與
文化意義，並能將相關分析方法應用於實際研究。
keywords: Course keywords: 石器、考古學、製作技術、分類、經濟文化
restrictions: 排除大學部1年級2年級

brief:
本課程是想像人類學的研究系列，將討論想像與圖像的相化問題。包括當代圖像的入侵、想像新體制的質問、相化他者與自我的拉
扯問題、相化的場域、形狀與時刻等。除了想像與圖像的知識系譜的認識，也將討論一些想像民族誌的圖像案例，以及進行田野調
查的實作練習。
keywords: Course keywords: 人類學、想像、圖像、相化、他者
restrictions: 排除大學部1年級2年級3年級

brief:
Conceptually, the Austronesian language family includes Micronesia, Melanesia, and Polynesia. While 
this course will discuss Taiwan and the Oceania region separately by theme, it will adopt the 
perspective of "Our Sea of Islands," shifting the political geography of Taiwan's Indigenous peoples 
from East Asia into Oceania. Through the concepts of food and bodily encounters, as well as 
wayfinding, the course will explore the food cultures and sensory concepts of the island communities 
in Oceania, facilitating an understanding of the differences and similarities between the Indigenous 
peoples of Taiwan and Oceania. 

Practically, this course will focus on discussions and hands-on activities related to food culture 
and the bodily issues it encompasses. The course will begin with Taiwan's Indigenous peoples and 
extend into the Oceania region, examining the essence of different foods, their ritual significance, 
social implications, sensory experiences,
keywords: Course keywords: Austronesian-speaking peoples/南島語族

brief:
This course is an undergraduate-level introduction to physical cosmology: the application of 
basic physics concepts to study the origin and evolution of the Universe. The emphasis will be on the 
"big picture" of how we learn about the structure and evolution of the universe from astronomical 
observations.
content: Course keywords: Cosmology, Astronomy, Astrophysics, Cosmological Observations, Galaxy Formation      課程說明 (Course Description)This course is an undergraduate-level introduction to the principles of cosmology: the study of the origin and evolution of the universe based on fundamental physics. The emphasis will be on astronomical observations, rather than particle physics. We will not use any mathematics more difficult than basic calculus. Although we will discuss concepts related to General Relativity, we will not do any GR calculations or derivations. The same is true for particle physics/quantum mechanics. There are no hard prerequisites for the course. However, you are expected to have a sound grasp of fundamental undergraduate physics at the 2nd-year level or above. You should understand the fundamental concepts of Newtonian gravity, special relativity and electromagnetic radiation (i.e. electron energy levels, the absorption and emission of photons) at the level of undergraduate "General Physics". Previous courses in basic astronomy will be extremely helpful.The course will be taught entirely in English, but you will be assessed on your understanding of the physical concepts, not your English ability. There will be a Mandarin-speaking TA.教學進度 (Syllabus)By the end of the course you should be able to:- Describe the principles of how distances to astronomical objects (like galaxies) are determined;- Describe the fundamental observational evidence for the expansion of the universe;- Understand the theoretical connection between the expansion of the universe and its contents;- Work with simple mathematic models of the expansion and understand how those models can be tested by observations;- Explain the origin and importance of the cosmic microwave background;- Describe the processes thought to have occurred in the first few minutes of the Universe, including "nucleosynthesis";- Explain the concepts of dark matter, dark energy and cosmic inflation;- Tell the (qualitative) story of how cosmic structures like stars and galaxies formed;- Appreciate some important open questions in modern cosmology.This course can be considered as a primer for the graduate course in cosmology offered by the Institute of Astronomy. This undergraduate course will not cover the practical, quantitative  mathematical framework needed to describe the formation and evolution of  structure, and to match cosmological observations to models. Frontier topics in cosmology will be covered only in a descriptive way, without calculations. 成績考核 (Evaluation)The exact evaluation method may be adapted depending on the class size, but will involve several homework assignments and a final exam.AI Policy: "有條件開放"Summary: AI use is acceptable as a supplement to learning, but answers to assessments must be your own work, and will be marked down for clear and uncritical use of AI tools. Use of AI in written assessments is discouraged and any such use must be clearly declared. Expect to be challenged to explain and prove your understanding if you hand in work suspected of being generated by AI without critical thought.Details: Using generative AI to help with your study is at least not worse than asking your classmates or reading random websites. There is no problem  with talking to your classmates (or AI) about the lectures or homework  assignments. You should not just accept what you are told, but always do your best to "absorb" and double-check any information on your own, and make sure you have a good "grip" on the ideas. Once you've learned about something from an AI chatbot, you should at  least try getting it to ask you some questions to test your understanding.This course involves some written assessment. Your answers to assessment  questions should *always* be your own, because the whole point of assessment is is to demonstrate to the instructor what *you* understand. Your answers to assessment questions should not come from your classmates, so they should not come from AI either. Some students use AI to "help with English". This course is not an English test, so there is absolutely no need to do that. The official language of the course is "broken English".  Your own honest answer in poor English is much better than someone else's answer in perfectly written English.教學方式 (Teaching Method)The course will be taught in a classical way, with weekly in-person lectures and recommendations for self-study. Basic lecture notes will be provided, but you are expected to read one or more textbooks by yourself.參考書籍 (References)The primary textbook for the course will be:- Introduction to Cosmology, by Barbara Ryden, 2nd Edition (Cambridge University Press, 2016) https://doi.org/10.1017/9781316651087As a second (easier but less complete) textbook, I recommend:- An Introduction to Modern Cosmology, by Andrew Liddle (3rd/revised edition, Wiley, 2015)You may also consider:- A Course in Cosmology, from Theory to Practice, by Dragan Huterer, 1st Edition (Cambridge University Press, 2023) https://doi.org/10.1017/9781009070232This is basically a slightly more advanced and up-to-date version of Ryden.More references will be given at the start of the course.

brief:

brief:
This course is a graduate-level introduction to theories and observations of galaxy formation and 
evolution, in the concordance Dark Energy and Cold Dark Matter (LambdaCDM) cosmogony. It is a core 
course of the Institute for Astronomy graduate syllabus.
content: Course keywords: Astronomy, Astrophysics, Galaxy Observations, Galaxy Formation, Galaxy Evolution      課程說明 (Course Description)This course is a graduate-level introduction to the nature of galaxies -- what they are, where they come from, and how they change over time. These are major topics in astronomical research, building on knowledge from other areas such as cosmology and stellar astrophysics.The course is intended as a primer for graduate research. We will aim to cover a broad range of topics, rather than a rigorous mathematical treatment.PLEASE NOTE: The level will be suitable for graduate and senior undergraduate students whose major is Physics or Astrophysics. The course will assume an undergraduate background knowledge of astronomy.The course will be offered and assessed in English.The homework exercises will involve simple numerical equation-solving and graph-plotting tasks. Basic instruction in python will be provided.Students who have not previously taken a course in cosmology may find it helpful to follow the undergraduate "Introduction to Modern Cosmology" given by the same lecturer, although we will not consider more than the "big picture" of cosmology in this course.教學進度(Syllabus)The minimum syllabus is:1. Astronomical measurements and observational techniques2. Stars and stellar populations3. Describing the different types of galaxies4. The cosmological context of galaxy formation5. Galaxy "environments"6. Dark matter halo origins and structure7. The origin of galaxies, gas cooling8. Cold gas disks and star formation9. "Feedback" and chemical enrichment10. Gravitational dynamics11. Galaxy interactions and mergers12. Galaxy evolution over cosmic time13. Supermassive black holes14. Open problems in galaxy formation This course will be deliberately "simple" in assuming almost no prior knowledge.For the first time, there will be a second course in the Spring semester covering more advanced topics and details required for modern galaxy evolution research. Effectively they will be "part 1" and "part 2" of the same syllabus. The "part 2" advanced course will assume familiarity with all the topics covered here.教學方式 (Teaching Method)Lectures, reading assignments.成績考核 (Evaluation)Approximately 4 homework exercises and final quiz-style exam.指定用書 (Text Books)The reference textbook for this course will be:* "Dynamics and Astrophysics of Galaxies" by Jo Bovy (Princeton U. Press, 2026)https://galaxiesbook.org/We will not go through everything in this book, and we will not follow the chapters in the order they are presented (we will focus mostly on chapter 18).We will also make use of the classic textbook:* “An Introduction to Modern Astrophysics” (2nd ed.) by B. W. Carroll & D. A. Ostlie (2006, Pearson Addison-Wesley)Some alternative/additional textbooks about galaxies:* (Simple) Fundamentals of Galaxy Dynamics, Formation and Evolution by Ignacio Ferreras (2019, UCL Press). Free e-book: https://www.uclpress.co.uk/products/84078* (Advanced) “Galaxy Formation and Evolution” by H. Mo, S. White & F. van den Bosch(2010, Cambridge University Press)* (Advanced) “Galactic Astronomy” (2nd ed.) by J. Binney & M. Merrifield (2008, Princeton  University Press)For the cosmological background to the course, the following textbooks may be helpful:* “Introduction to Cosmology” (2nd Ed.) by Barbara Ryden (2016, Cambridge University Press)* “An Introduction to Modern Cosmology” (3rd Ed.) by Andrew Liddle  (2015, Wiley)

brief:
This is the weekly colloquium of the NTHU Institute of Astronomy. Talks in a wide range of fields in 
astronomy and astrophysics will be delivered by visiting speakers.
content: Course keywords: Colloquium, Seminar, Astronomy, Presentation Skills, Professional Development      課程說明 (Course Description)The weekly astronomy colloquium series provides excellent opportunities for students to gain insight into cutting-edge astronomical research, build connections with visiting speakers, and develop presentation skills by learning from experienced presenters. This course helps students cultivate a broad range of professional skills that are essential for careers in astronomy and beyond, including delivering and engaging with presentations, asking constructive questions, and interacting with colleagues who work on different topics and at different institutions. Interacting with visiting speakers also helps students learn not only about science, but also about diverse perspectives on life and work in the professional astronomy community.成績考核 (Evaluation)Grades for this course will be evaluated based on:1. Attendance (80%): Please sign in using the sign-up sheet provided by the TA for each colloquium.Students who attend all regular colloquia on Fridays during the semester will receive full credits in this category. Participation (20%): Students are encouraged to interact with the speakers and reflect on the colloquium. brief:
This course provides a structured forum for graduate students to present their research, develop 
professional-level scientific presentation skills, and become familiar with the breadth of ongoing 
research within the institute, fostering scientific discussion and potential collaboration.
content: Course keywords: Astronomy, Seminar, Presentation Skills, Professional Development      課程說明 (Course Description)Modern astronomical research is increasingly collaborative and interdisciplinary, spanning theory, observation, instrumentation, data science, and numerical simulation. Graduate students must not only develop deep expertise in their own research area, but also acquire the ability to communicate their work clearly to diverse audiences and engage constructively with work outside their immediate specialization.  This seminar course provides a structured environment in which students present their ongoing research to peers, postdoctoral researchers, and faculty, receive constructive feedback on scientific communication, and learn about current projects across the institute. The format emphasizes work-in-progress presentations, discussion, and methodological exchange, thereby strengthening the intellectual cohesion of the graduate program and supporting the professional development of students as researchers.  The course will:●	Develop effective oral scientific communication skills ●	Provide regular opportunities for students to present their own research ●	Expose students to the full range of research topics pursued within the institute ●	Foster critical scientific discussion and interaction ●	Encourage interdisciplinary thinking and collaboration among students and postdocsFormat: The first lecture would cover introduction to the seminar, expectations, and effective scientific presentations. Each of the remaining lectures would be composed of two presentations given by students as well as invited speakers (postdocs or faculties). Each presentation is 20-25 minutes plus 5-10 minutes for questions and discussions. Each presentation will be evaluated by the peers, the TA, and the instructor. The students are encouraged to ask questions to receive participation points.  The class is a required graduate research seminar for all astronomy MSc and PhD students (two semesters required for MSc students and four semesters for PhD students). However, in the field of astronomy alone, nearly 40 new papers are published every day. It is a significant amount of work to keep up with this flood of papers. The purpose of this course is to train students to efficiently read and understand the essence of new research papers within a limited amount of time. Students will spend no more than one hour reading a paper of their choice and will then take turns presenting a short  summary in 10 minutes. The focus will be on understanding the main points rather than getting into the details. It is not necessary to read every single detail of the paper. Additionally, other students in the class will have a valuable opportunity to learn about the latest papers while listening to the speaker. After each presentation, the instructor will teach a relevant physics concept related to the reviewed paper.The course will take place every Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday from 12:10 pm to 1 pm. During each session, three papers will be reviewed. Therefore, over the course of one semester, we will review almost 100 papers. By the end of the semester, students will be familiar with the latest advancements in astronomy.Previous knowledge is not required. We will focus on learning key concepts of astronomy as they arise in research papers. This bottom-up approach reflects the practical and realistic nature of everyday research life. brief:
Computational astrophysics is being reshaped by large language models (LLMs) and AI coding tools, 
which are changing how scientific software is written, tested, and maintained. This graduate course 
teaches AI-assisted coding as a practical methodology and applies it directly to core problems in 
computational astrophysics.

LLMs operate to use them deliberately rather than superstitiously. Second, and primarily, students 
will apply AI-assisted workflows to develop, debug, and validate real astrophysical codes, from a 
simple orbit integrator up to a fluid solver and a machine-learning project.

brief:
Molecular Simulation and Modeling (MD I) is the first half of a year-long sequence that introduces the 
theoretical foundations of molecular simulations. The course focuses on helping students understand 
key concepts behind molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of biomolecules. Topics include statistical 
mechanics and several widely used ideas and methods in molecular simulations.
Although modern software makes simulations easy to perform, correctly interpreting and troubleshooting 
simulations still requires understanding the basic principles on which these methods are built. This 
course therefore explains these principles clearly and systematically.
content: Course keywords: molecular simulation, molecular dynamics simulation, statistical mechanics, numerical methods, optimization, sampling methods, free energy, 分子模擬, 分子動力學模擬, 統計力學, 數值方法, 最適化, 取樣方法, 自由能      ● 課程說明(Course Description)Molecular Simulation and Modeling (MD I) introduces the theoretical foundations of molecular simulations, with a primary focus on molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of biomolecules. The course covers essential concepts such as statistical mechanics, energy minimization, integrators, constraints, and temperature and pressure control. These topics form the basis for understanding how molecular simulations are constructed, how they evolve in time, and how their results should be interpreted.Although modern software makes running simulations straightforward, correctly analyzing and troubleshooting them still requires a clear understanding of the underlying principles. This course therefore explains these principles in a systematic and accessible manner, emphasizing the reasoning behind commonly used simulation techniques.By the end of this course, students will be able to:Understand the statistical-mechanical principles underlying molecular dynamics simulationsExplain the role of energy minimization, integrators, and constraints in MDDescribe how temperature and pressure control are implemented and interpreted● 指定用書(Text Books)Lecture notes will be provided in class.● 參考書籍(References)1. Daan Frenkel, Berend Smit “Understanding Molecular Simulation: From Algorithms to Applications” (Computational Science Series, Vol 1).● 教學方式(Teaching Method)Lectures (theory-based instruction).● 教學進度(Syllabus)This course is part of a year-long sequence on the theoretical foundations of molecular simulations. The actual order and depth of topics may vary each year depending on the pace and background of the class. MD I introduces the fundamental concepts, and MD II continues with topics that build upon this background. brief:
本課程介紹生醫工程光學與顯微影像分析之核心概念，涵蓋光學成像原理、顯微鏡系統架構、螢光與多模態影像技術，以及影像處理與分
析方法。課程結合理論講授、文獻討論與應用，培養學生掌握生醫影像擷取、定量分析與結果判讀能力，並進一步連結疾病診斷、細胞觀
察與醫學研究等實際應用，建立跨領域研究與創新發展基礎。
This course introduces the core concepts of biomedical engineering optics and microscopic image 
analysis, covering optical imaging principles, microscope system architecture, fluorescence and 
multimodal imaging techniques, and image processing and analysis methods. Combining theoretical 
lectures, literature discussions, and applications, the course cultivates students' abilities in 
biomedical image acquisition, quantitative analysis, and result interpretation. It further connects 
to practical applications such as disease diagnosis, cell observation, and medical research, 
establishing a foundation for interdisciplinary research and innovative development.
keywords: Course keywords: Biomedical Optics; Microscopic Imaging; Optical Imaging; Fluorescence Microscopy; Image Analysis

brief:
本課程介紹柔性生醫光電感測之核心原理、材料、元件製作與系統整合，涵蓋柔性基板、光電感測機制、BioMEMS微製程、可
穿戴與即時
監測技術，以及AI輔助訊號分析與判讀。課程將結合理論講授、文獻討論與應用案例，培養學生掌握生醫感測器設計、資料
處理與臨床轉
譯能力，並能進一步發想智慧醫療、健康監測與精準診斷之創新解決方案。
This course introduces the core principles, materials, component fabrication, and system integration 
of flexible biomedical optoelectronic sensing. It covers flexible substrates, optoelectronic sensing 
mechanisms, BioMEMS microfabrication, wearable and real-time monitoring technologies, and AI-
assisted signal analysis and interpretation. The course combines theoretical lectures, literature 
discussions, and application case studies to cultivate students' skills in biomedical sensor design, 
data processing, and clinical translation, and to further develop innovative solutions for smart 
healthcare, health monitoring, and precision diagnosis.
keywords: Course keywords: Flexible biomedical optoelectronic sensing; BioMEMS; Wearable sensing; Artificial intelligence analytics; Smart healthcare

brief:
This course introduces soft materials from an engineering perspective, emphasizing how to design, 
process, characterize, and apply polymers, hydrogels, colloids, emulsions, and other soft systems in 
biomedical, manufacturing, and electronic applications.
Learning goals
1.	identify major classes of soft materials and where they are used
2.	connect material composition and processing to performance
3.	interpret common characterization data such as rheology, swelling, and mechanical tests
4.	choose suitable soft materials for a practical engineering problem
5.	analyze case studies in biomaterials, coatings, printing, and soft devices

brief:
This course is designed for first- and second-year BMES bachelor students, aiming to develop 
technical English skills specific to the discipline of Biomedical Engineering. The course will focus 
on improving students’ abilities in listening, reading, writing, and speaking. By the end of the 
course, each student will be expected to give an oral presentation, demonstrating their ability to 
organize content, utilize graphics and visual aids, and present information in a clear and logical 
manner.
content: Course keywords: English for Specific Purposes, English for Academic Purposes, Biomedical Engineering English, Technical English      一、課程說明(Course Description) This course is designed for first- and second-year BMES bachelor's students and aims to develop technical English skills relevant to the field of Biomedical Engineering while strengthening students’ engagement with the international academic community. The course will focus on enhancing students’ listening, reading, writing, and speaking abilities through content drawn from engineering, science, and medical science, helping them build familiarity with technical terminology.In addition to technical language development, the course will introduce and explore important contemporary issues in biomedical engineering, including gender inequality in clinical practice, research, and the workplace; ethical considerations in clinical trials and preclinical animal studies; and the social and environmental responsibilities associated with engineering and healthcare innovation.By the end of the course, each student will be expected to deliver an oral presentation that demonstrates their ability to organize content effectively, make appropriate use of graphics and visual aids, and communicate information in a clear, logical, and professional manner.二、教學方式(Teaching Method) Various topics within the field of Biomedical Engineering will be introduced. Technical information will be delivered through lectures, reading materials (text), and multimedia videos (listening). Each week, a list of relevant vocabulary will be provided. Throughout the semester, in-class exercises will facilitate practice through pair conversations (speaking practice), group discussions, written exercises, and opportunities for presentations.三、教學進度(Syllabus) R26; Intro to Biomedical EngineeringR26; BiomechanicsR26; Medical ImagingR26; Medical Devices and developmentsR26; Biomaterials and Tissue EngineeringR26; NanotechnologyR26; Computational systems biologyR26; Genetic EngineeringR26; Academic Writing (Reports, Journal articles, Thesis): structure and styleR26; Academic Presentations skills (Oral, Posters): effective methods and medium utilization四、成績考核(Evaluation)  - 60% class attendance and participation - 20% in-class exercises - 20% 5-min presentation

brief:
1) 瞭解臨床醫學基本觀念及其相關疾病的表徵和治療重點
2) 內科、外科、急診、急救、婦產科、兒科等相關科學的基本介紹
3) 瞭解相關醫學術語、一般醫學知識、及臨床評估之意義
4) 瞭解並落實生醫科技領域當中基礎與臨床之結合
content: Course keywords: 臨床醫學(clinical medicine)，醫學知識(medical knowledge)，生醫科技(biomedical technology)，創新臨床醫療(medical innovation)，轉譯醫學(translational medicine)      課程說明  介紹臨床醫學的基本觀念，討論和其相關的議題，瞭解各科疾病，諸如:內科、外科、婦產科、小兒科、急救等之臨床表徵及其治療上的重點，當今治療面臨的問題，並學習與日常生活習習相關的醫療知識，最後展望未來醫學發展，推展生醫科技領域當中基礎與臨床之結合。  將專業艱澀的醫學知識，由受過醫環系教育的醫師整理介紹給醫環系或相關科系學生，藉以了解醫環系的研究如何在臨床醫學中找到相對應的研究題目。或是藉由課程的修習，能增加醫學常識，促進自己及周遭親朋好友的健康。指定用書(Text Books)：臨床醫學概論 華杏出版社 作者：洪敏元教學進度上課日期：1. 9/9, 16, 23, 30   10/7, 14, 21, 28   11/4, 18, 25   12/2, 9, 163. 停課：   11/11: 全校運動大會(停課一天)   12/23: 期末考週4. 課程內容： 心臟科：主動脈剝離、 心肌梗塞、心律不整、高血壓、心導管 眼科：近視雷射、視網膜剝離、兒童視力矯正、結膜炎、青光眼 腸胃科：胃痛、吐血、肝硬化、胃潰瘍、胃癌、幽門螺旋桿菌、B型肝炎 放射：Ｘ光、電腦斷層、磁振造影、超音波、血管攝影 外科：手術基礎技巧教學、 牙科：齲齒（蛀牙）、植牙、齒列矯正、牙周病、智齒阻生 一般外科: 肝癌、胃癌、乳癌、胰臟癌、急性膽囊炎、腹股溝疝氣、急性闌尾炎 婦產科: 子宮出血、月經異常、經痛、骨盆器官脫垂、安全期、巧克力囊腫、懷孕、自然產、剖腹產 急診科: CPR 、傷口處置、AED 教學、胸腹部外傷急症、燒燙傷、中毒 皮膚科：美容醫學、鳳凰電波拉皮、肉毒桿菌、黑頭粉刺、青春痘 大腸直腸外科: 痔瘡、血便、大腸癌、大腸鏡、糞便篩檢、達文西手術、肛門痛 小兒科: 新生兒、早產兒、兒童發展遲緩、異位性皮膚炎、尿布疹、輪狀病毒感染、疫苗 整形外科： 形體美容、重建本課程無涉及AI使用 Not applicable成績考核１．出席＋隨堂考：85％,  ２．期末報告：5 ％,  ３．課堂抽問：10%

brief:
With the internet of things (IoT) rapid development and advanced devices that can monitor a myriad 
of 
biometric parameters, wearable biomedical device has gained the interest of physicians and 
researchers due to the benefits that could be associated with long-term monitoring of patients for 
healthcare. The course will provide students with introduction to wearable biomedical devices and 
its principle is based on the latest academic research and commercial biomedical product 
development. 

The course will  guide students to see the overview of the current wearable biomedical devices and 
help them to train  their scientific thinking from initial unmet needs to device design, and further 
fabrication technologies for wearable biomedical devices.

brief:
This course introduces the fundamental concepts and applications of magnetic resonance imaging.  
The concepts include spin behavior, NMR signals, hardware, pulse sequence, and k-space. The technical 
applications regarding fast scan, parallel imaging, and artifacts will be covered in this course. We 
will also introduce some of the clinical applications, e.g., fMRI, angiography, diffusion, and 
perfusion.

The course will cover three biomedical imaging techniques: Ultrasound, Optical, and Optoacoustics. 
Fundamentals physics, signal detection, and image formation for each modality will be discussed, 
followed by their applications. An emphasis will be placed on the contrasting and complementary 
nature between the first two: ultrasound and optical methods. This will lead the discussion into the 
third topic of photoacoustic techniques and applications, where the characteristics, highlights, and 
current limitations will be explored. In the last portion of this course, students will have a 
chance to exercise logical reasoning and creative problem solving skill in anticipating and 
resolving potential problems
content: Course keywords: Medical diagnostics, Biological Imaging, Ultrasound imaging, Optical technique, Photoacoustic/ Optoacoustic imaging, Image processing，醫療診斷, 生物影像，超音波成像，光學技術，光聲成像，影像處理      一、課程說明(Course Description)The course will start with a revision on the motivations of biomedical imaging, along with common techniques and challenges. Then, we will zoom in on ultrasound imaging techniques: from acoustic wave propagation in tissue to the understanding of transducers and image formation. As we explore system designs and their applications, we will denote the characteristics and limitations of the method. We will follow this by covering optical imaging. As we go from fundamentals to systems and applications, and finally to challenges and outlook, discussion will be steered towards its features complementary to those of acoustic techniques. Finally, the last third section of the course will be on the study of photoacoustic (optoacoustic) methods, where we combine optical excitation and acoustic detection. 二、參考書籍 (References)- Biomedical Optics: Principles and Imaging by Hsin-I Wu and Lihong V. 6.	Phase diagrams 
7.	Chemical equilibrium 

After this class, you should be able to use the methods of equilibrium thermodynamics to describe the properties and processes of 
macroscopic systems.

brief:
Net-zero carbon emissions by 2050 is necessary to limit the global temperature increase within 1.5 
C and avoid irreversible damage from global warming.  Fossil fuel power plants are responsible for 
the most carbon emissions among the anthropogenic sources.  Carbon capture and sequestration (CCS) 
is an essential technology to decarbonize power generation and achieve the net-zero carbon 
emission target.  This course will focus on the CCS technology development in the context of 
mitigating the global warming.  In this class, the students will be expected to learn:
1.	The greenhouse gas sources and the mitigation methods 
2.	The low-emission power generation technology 
3.	The carbon capture and sequestration technology with amine scrubbing
4.	Current status of carbon capture in industry

brief:
Materials science investigates the microstructure of materials and their physical, chemical and 
mechanical properties. This course is divided into three parts: (1) Microstructure of materials, 
atomic bonding and coordination, atomic arrangement in crystals and crystal defects (especially the 
theory of vacancies and dislocations). (2) Thermodynamics and kinetics of materials Science: phase 
diagrams, solid diffusion and heat treatment, which are the basis for controlling and changing the 
microstructure of materials. (3) Properties of materials: discussing the physical, chemical, and 
mechanical properties of metals, ceramics, composite materials, and semiconductors.

brief:
This course provides an introduction to polymer materials and processing technologies, with an 
emphasis on the relationship between polymer structure, material properties, and processing behavior. 
Topics include polymer classification, molecular structure, crystallinity, mechanical behavior, 
viscoelasticity, creep, stress relaxation, and melt flow characteristics. The course further 
introduces major polymer processing methods, including extrusion, injection molding, additive 
manufacturing, advanced packaging, and fiber-reinforced composite processing. Students will learn how 
processing conditions influence polymer flow, deformation, material structure, and final product 
performance. Applications of computer-aided engineering (CAE) in polymer processing and packaging will 
also be discussed.
content: Course keywords: 高分子材料, 高分子流變性質, 高分子機械性質，模具設計，電腦輔助工程分析, Injection molding, extrusion, polymer, fiber reinforced composites，塑膠加工, 先進封裝      一、課程說明(Course Description)本課程旨在提供學生對高分子材料與其加工技術的全面認識，內容涵蓋從材料基礎、機械行為、流變性質，到實際加工應用，包含在先進封裝技術的應用。課程前半段將介紹天然與合成高分子材料的基本聚合反應、熱塑性與熱固性塑膠、彈性體等分類，並深入探討聚合度、結晶度與無定形特性對材料性能的影響。此外，也將說明分子鏈結構與材料應用之間的關聯。接續將探討高分子材料的機械行為，包括其在應力與應變下展現的彈性、塑性與黏彈性特性，並進一步說明潛變、應力鬆弛與疲勞等時間相關的力學行為。接下來透過高分子熔體的流動行為學習溫度、剪切速率與分子量對流動性的影響，並認識黏彈性理論與基本流變測試儀器。課程後半著重於實務加工技術，包括擠出成型（單螺桿與雙螺桿）、射出成型與模具設計，並進一步介紹高分子混煉與共混、纖維強化複合材料等應用技術。在半導體封裝方面，將說明CoWoS、FOWLP等先進封裝技術對材料性能與製程的挑戰。此外，也將介紹電腦輔助工程（CAE）在高分子加工與封裝中的應用，以提升製程模擬與產品設計效率。本課程適合對高分子材料有興趣，並希望深入了解其於各項製程領域應用的學生，為未來從事材料開發、製程優化奠定扎實基礎。This course provides students with a comprehensive introduction to polymer materials and processing technologies. Topics include polymer classification, structure–property relationships, mechanical behavior, melt flow characteristics, and practical processing applications.The first part of the course introduces thermoplastics, thermosets, elastomers, and natural and synthetic polymers, with emphasis on how molecular structure, degree of polymerization, crystallinity, and amorphous characteristics influence material properties. The course also covers the mechanical behavior of polymers, including elasticity, plasticity, viscoelasticity, creep, and stress relaxation.The second part focuses on polymer processing technologies and applications, including extrusion, injection molding, additive manufacturing, advanced packaging, and fiber-reinforced composite processing. Students will learn how polymer melts flow, deform, and solidify during processing, and how processing conditions affect material structure and final properties. Applications of computer-aided engineering (CAE) in polymer processing and packaging will also be introduced.This course is suitable for students interested in polymer materials, materials processing, and engineering applications, and provides a foundation for further study in polymer processing, composite materials, process design, and materials development.二、指定用書(Text Books) 1. content: Course keywords: pump, flow meters, heat exchanger, dryer, distillation, leaching, extraction, absorption, adsorption, mechanical separation      一、	課程說明(Course Description) This course is designed to provide basic understanding of transport phenomena and unit operations for graduate students with a non-chemical engineering undergraduate background. It is divided into two parts. The first part takes 9 weeks to cover physical properties (viscosity, conductivity, diffusivity) and (momentum, energy, mass) transport mechanisms, and shell balance techniques for solving physical quantity (velocity, temperature, concentration) distributions in simple transport problems. The second part focuses on several key unit operations such as fluid delivery, mixing, separation and heating and drying that are critical for students to learn so that they can apply some basic knowledge and skill in this area when they start to work in domestic plants.二、指定用書(Text Books) Bird, R.B., W.E. brief:
This course will cover the principles and applications of small angle X-ray and neutron scattering, 
which are important tools for exploring the nanostructures, thermodynamics and dynamics of matters.  
The objective is to provide the students a solid background on these techniques, which may be 
helpful for their research in related subjects.  The topics covered in this course are outlined as 
follows. 

1. Basics of X-ray and Neutron Scattering
2. Small Angle Scattering
2. Applications to Polymer Blends and Block Copolymers
4. Application to Amorphous Polymers
5. Study of Surfaces and Interfaces
6. Inelastic Scattering for Dynamics Studies

The materials taught in class will be based largely on the book of:  
R. J. Roe, “Methods of X-ray and Neutron Scattering in Polymer Science”, Oxford University Press 
(2000)

Two exams will be held and a final written report is required.

brief:
This course aims to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the theoretical and 
practical aspects of computational modeling in chemical and materials systems. Through this course, 
students will develop proficiency in computational thinking, which involves the analysis of 
characteristic scales (time and length) relevant to the problems of interest, and the utilization of 
associated computational tools.
content: Course keywords: 電腦模擬、原子尺度模擬、第一原理計算、分子動力學模擬      一、課程說明(Course Description)This course aims to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the theoretical and practical aspects of computational modeling in chemical and materials systems. Through this course, students will develop proficiency in computational thinking, which involves the analysis of characteristic scales (time and length) relevant to the problems of interest, and the utilization of associated computational tools.This course is designed for students in chemical engineering. Therefore, the course emphasizes a hands-on approach where students are requested to investigate three classic types of systems in chemical engineering via computational approaches:1. Organic semiconductors (ab-initio gas-phase computations: MO, IE/EA, vibrational spectroscopy, thermodynamic properties (harmonic approximation), excited-state properties)2. Surface catalytic reactions (ab-initio solid-state simulations: band structure, work function, adsorption energy, volcano plot, activation energy barrier)3. Predictions of thermodynamic properties (classical force-field molecular dynamics simulations: vapor-liquid equilibrium, activity coefficient)Overall, the course is designed to equip students with the necessary skills and knowledge to apply computational techniques to real-world problems in the field of chemical and materials systems.This course is a bit demanding, and it is strongly recommended that the students know some basic knowledge of:1. Quantum chemistry/ quantum mechanics2. Python3. Thermodynamics and statistical thermodynamics4. Solid-state physicsThis course places a strong emphasis on pre-reading assigned materials and in-class discussions. This component will account for 25% of the total grade.二、指定用書(Text Books)No三、參考書籍(References)Quantum chemistry and quantum mechanics:1. Molecular Quantum Mechanics / Peter Atkins2. A Chemist's Guide to Density Functional Theory / Koch and Max C. Holthausen2. Time-Dependent Density-Functional Theory: Concepts and Applications / Carsten A. UllrichMolecular dynamics simulations (MD)1. Understanding Molecular Simulation: From Algorithms to Applications / Berend Smit and Daan Frenkel2. Computer Simulation of Liquids / D. J. Tildesley and M.P. Allen四、教學方式(Teaching Method)Lectures (2 courses) + hands-on session (1+ course)五、教學進度(Syllabus)1. (5 weeks) Organic semiconductors (ab-initio gas-phase computations: MO, IE/EA, vibrational spectroscopy, thermodynamic properties (harmonic approximation), excited-state properties)2. (4 weeks) Surface catalytic reactions (ab-initio solid-state simulations: band structure, work function, adsorption energy, volcano plot, activation energy barrier)3. (4 weeks) Predictions of thermodynamic properties (classical force-field molecular dynamics simulations: vapor-liquid equilibrium, activity coefficient)4. (3 weeks) Final presentation六、成績考核(Evaluation)Quiz and in-class performance 15%4 Homework sets 60% Final Presentation 25%七、可連結之網頁位址No八、AI使用規則1. 修讀本門課程之學生應注意本門課不得繳交使用生成式人工智慧所產出的作業、報告或個人心得。若經查核發現，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。2. 修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。

1.選擇新奇有趣及生活化的教材：使用原文教學實驗課本，加強學生閱讀外語文章及熟悉化學專業用語。選新奇有趣及生活 
化的實驗(如從天然物裡取得有用的純化物、生化藥物抗生素之全合成、化學鑑定所使用魯米諾的合成及放光等)，激發學生
做實驗的興趣並能更有切身的體會。 
2.嚴謹扎實的實驗訓練及經驗的傳承：有機實驗基本技巧是所有實驗的根本，加強訓練基礎技巧。督促學生邊實驗邊思考問 
題及預判可能發展性，才能養成其從事研究之獨立思考能力。加強實作經驗的傳承，連想思考研究方向及知道如何開始著手 
解決問題。
3.藥品安全與增添特殊器材增廣見識：養成學生閱讀藥品性質的習慣，隨時閱讀該藥品性質及知悉其危險性，增加使用藥品 
安全性。增添新器材的使用，如短管蒸餾、冷凝管、乾浴器等應用等，讓實驗更多元化更活用器材的運用度。

brief:
無機化學為有機化學的相對延伸，探討週期表中所有元素（除了碳與氫）及有機金屬化合物中碳的化學特性。無機化學的領域極
為廣泛，在現代科學發展應用上愈趨重要。例如有機金屬化學涵蓋對金屬-碳化合物的鍵結與有機反應的催化機制等研究；生物
無機化學為跨生物化學與無機化學領域的研究；環境化學則包含有機化學與無機化學二大領域。本課程將廣泛介紹現代無機化學
中各項主題，並著眼在基本知識的學習和思考能力的啟發，以作為未來深入研究的基石。

brief:
本課程旨在培養學生對化學領域最新發展與前沿知識的理解，並透過系統性查詢、閱讀與整理相關文獻，熟悉最新研究方向與趨
勢。課程同時著重於簡報製作與口頭表達能力的訓練，使學生能清晰、有效地傳達化學知識，進而激發研究興趣並奠定未來學術

content: Course keywords: 有機化學 organic chemistry, 無機化學 inorganic chemistry, 批判性思考 critical thinking, 學術口頭表達 academic oral presentation, 文獻探討 literature review      課程說明 (Course Description)本課程旨在透過化學專業情境培養學生之學術英語能力，並聚焦於有機化學與無機化學之最新研究發展。學生將學習如何搜尋、閱讀、評估與整理近期學術文獻，掌握當前研究趨勢與前沿議題。透過口頭報告、結構化討論及文獻探討，學生將訓練以英語清楚且專業地表達科學概念。課程亦強調批判性思考、證據導向論述、科學推理，以及學術討論中的即時應答能力，同時鼓勵跨領域連結與研究興趣探索，作為未來學術發展之基礎。本課程採三人小組合作模式，每次由一位學生進行專題口頭報告，一位學生擔任主持人引導討論，另一位學生負責整理問題與討論紀錄。其餘學生亦以三人小組方式參與，每場報告後進行 5 分鐘討論，並提出至少一個問題作為全班討論基礎。教學方式 (Teaching Methods)1. 口頭報告每位學生須選擇一篇與有機化學或無機化學相關之期刊論文，經授課教師核准後進行報告。論文選擇條件：期刊 Impact Factor > 4發表年份：2024–2026同儕審查之研究型論文口頭報告14天前，需準備3–5頁投影片，與老師討論報告內容與架構。口頭報告要求：報告時間 25 分鐘開場重點摘要 3–5 分鐘含問答討論時間2. 課程進行方式本課程採分組專題討論方式進行。學生以三人為一組，每次報告由一組負責，其中一人擔任口頭報告者，進行 25 分鐘專題文獻報告；一人擔任主持人，負責介紹主題、掌握時間、引導討論與協助問答進行；另一人擔任問題整理者，負責記錄各組提問、現場討論內容與課後彙整。每場報告結束後，其餘同學亦以三人為一組進行 5 分鐘小組討論。各組需根據報告內容提出至少一個問題，問題可包含文獻理解、研究方法、數據詮釋、實驗設計、研究限制或未來延伸等面向。各組提出之問題將作為課堂討論基礎，並納入課程參與評量。本課程強調學生不僅需具備文獻閱讀與口頭表達能力，也需學習主持學術討論、提出具批判性之問題，並透過同儕互動深化對研究內容的理解。透過報告、主持、提問與討論紀錄等不同角色，學生將培養科學溝通、批判思考與團隊合作能力。3. 文獻探討與摘要寫作學生須於報告前一週繳交所選論文與摘要，供教師與同學預先閱讀。4. 教師與同儕回饋報告與討論表現將由教師與同儕共同評分，重視學術內容深度、表達能力與專業態度。成績考核 (Evaluation)1. 簡報表現 (Presentation Skills)：50%2. 口頭表達與儀態 (Delivery & Professionalism)：10%3. 問答表現 (Answers to Questions)：10%4. 提問與參與討論 (Question Raising & Participation)：10%5. 文獻選擇與摘要品質 (Paper Selection & Abstract Quality)：5%6. 出席率與準時性 (Attendance & Punctuality)：5%7. 同儕評分 (Peer Evaluation)：10%AI 使用規則 (Select Applicable AI Usage Policy Policy)有條件開放，學生可使用生成式 AI 協助下列事項：文法修正與語言潤飾；專業詞彙提升；簡報架構發想；背景知識整理；發音與口語練習輔助。學生須於簡報中明確註明 AI 使用方式與範圍。學生不得使用 AI 進行以下行為：捏造數據、文獻或研究結果；錯誤詮釋論文內容；取代本人閱讀原始論文；未經實質修改即直接提交 AI 生成內容。所有作業之正確性、原創性與學術誠信，仍由學生本人負責。

brief:
This course aims to introduce the spectroscopic methods, their corresponding fundemental theory and 
data interpretation. The primary focus will be on three types of spectroscopy: infrared (IR), UV-Vis, 
and Raman. Students will explore various dimensions of these methods, including steady-state, time-
resolved and spatially-resolved (microscopy). They will learn the principles behind instrumental 
designs and the physical significance of each spectrum. The ultimate goal is to connect foundational 
knowledge of quantum chemistry, quantum dynamics, photophysics, and photochemistry to instrumental 
design and spectral analysis.

The purpose of this seminar course is to develop essential skills for graduate research in analytical chemistry. Students will learn to 
critically read and evaluate recent scientific literature, organize scientific information, give oral presentations in English, answer 
questions, and participate actively in scientific discussions.
content: Course keywords: Analytical Chemistry, Literature Search, Scientific Presentation, Scientific Discussion, Critical Thinking      課程說明 (Course Description)本課程旨在訓練學生閱讀與分析近期分析化學文獻，並培養科學簡報、批判性思考及學術討論能力。學生將選擇近期研究論文，以英文進行口頭報告，並參與課堂問答與討論。This course aims to develop students’ skills in reading and critically evaluating recent literature in analytical chemistry, as well as scientific presentation and discussion. Students will give oral presentations in English and actively participate in class discussions.指定用書 (Text Books)無指定教科書。No designated textbook.參考書籍 (References)以近五年內發表於 SCI/SCIE 收錄期刊，且與分析化學相關之原始研究論文為主。所選論文須具有明確的分析化學內容或方法上的創新性，不接受發表於掠奪性期刊（predatory journals）之論文。所有報告文獻須經授課教師確認。Recent original research articles published within the past five years in reputable SCI/SCIE-indexed journals related to analytical chemistry. Articles published in predatory journals will not be accepted. All selected articles must be approved by the instructor.教學方式 (Teaching Methods)課程包括教師講授、文獻研讀、學生口頭報告及課堂討論。學生須閱讀並理解所選論文，以英文進行科學簡報，並回答教師及同學的問題。Lectures, literature study, student presentations, and class discussion. Students are expected to understand the selected articles, present them clearly in English, and participate actively in discussion.教學進度 (Course Schedule)Week 1 — Course Introduction課程介紹、評分方式、文獻選擇原則及報告要求。Week 2 — Literature Search and Article Selection如何搜尋、篩選及評估適合書報討論的分析化學文獻。Week 3 — How to Give a Scientific Presentation科學簡報的架構、研究背景與研究問題的介紹、結果呈現、科學論述及問答技巧。Week 4 — Effective PowerPoint for Scientific Presentations科學簡報投影片的製作，包括版面、文字、圖表、資訊呈現及常見問題。Week 5 onward — Student Presentations and Discussion學生依排定順序進行報告。每次報告後進行問答、討論及回饋。The detailed presentation schedule will be adjusted according to class size and course progress.成績考核 (Evaluation)Literature search and article selection: 15%Scientific presentation and slide quality: 30%Understanding and critical evaluation of the literature: 30%Questions and answers: 15%Class participation and discussion: 10%請假依《國立清華大學學生請假辦法》辦理。若因請假無法進行原訂報告，請事先通知授課教師，並另行安排補報告。Absence and leave will follow the NTHU Student Leave Regulations. Students who are unable to give a scheduled presentation should notify the instructor in advance and arrange a make-up presentation.AI 使用規則 (AI Usage Policy)有條件開放使用 (Conditionally open)可使用生成式 AI 協助英文文法修正、文字潤飾及簡報架構整理，但不得取代學生本人對原始論文的閱讀、理解及批判性分析。學生須自行確認所有科學內容及引用資料的正確性，並對報告內容負責。Generative AI may be used for language editing and organization of presentation materials, but it should not replace the student's own reading, understanding, and critical evaluation of the original literature. Students are responsible for the accuracy of all scientific content and references.與課程相關的網站 (Course-related Website)NTHU eeclasshttps://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw/

brief:
The organic Synthesis I course will cover enolate chemistry with C-C bond formations through 
alkylation and additions to aldehydes and 
ketones as well as nucleophilic acyl substitution. Some functional group interversions through 
substitution chemistry will be discussed. 
Due to functional group compatibility issues, suitable functional group protections and subsequent 
deprotections are required. 
Electrophilic additions to C=C and CC triple bonds will be discussed along with stereo- selectivity 
issues. Diels-Alder type 
cycloadditions, rearrangement chemistry and thermal elimination will be covered. Final discussion of 
pericyclic reaction will be centered 
on electrocyclization.

Pearson.________________________________________教學方式 (Teaching Methods)1.書報討論:每位學生需輪流選擇並報告一篇高影響力的無機化學研究論文，使用PowerPoint進行展示。報告後，全班參與討論，教師提供專業建議。2.團隊討論:每次課程將分小組進行深入探討，以提高學生分析問題的深度和廣度。3.反饋與改進:學生在報告後收到教師及同學的建議，並撰寫反思報告（Reflection Report），以提升學習效果。________________________________________教學進度 (Course Schedule)週次	內容	備註第1週	課程介紹與書報選題指導	說明報告要求與評分標準第2週	無機化學基礎研究介紹	由教師說明第3週	學生報告1：催化與小分子活化研究	進行課後討論與反饋第4週	學生報告2：金屬有機框架（MOF）的設計與應用	第5週	學生報告3：無機錯合物的電子結構與光譜分析	第6週	學生報告4：均相與異相催化的機制研究	第7週	學生報告5：主族元素的功能性應用	第8週	期中回顧與改進建議	集中討論，總結學生表現與問題第9週	學生報告6：過渡金屬配合物的光催化應用	第10週	學生報告7：生物無機化學中的金屬離子功能研究	第11週	學生報告8：非傳統配體設計與其催化應用	第12週	學生報告9：固態無機化學的結構與性能研究	第13週	學生報告10：新穎無機材料的合成與應用	第14週	期末總結與學生報告改進討論	第15週	專題報告總結	由學生進行最終報告，並提交反思報告第16週	課程總結與結束	綜合評價與回顧課程目標達成情況________________________________________成績考核 (Evaluation)1.	文獻閱讀報告：50%2.	課堂參與與討論表現：30%3.	期末專題書面報告：20%________________________________________採用下AI 使用規則 (Select Applicable AI Usage Policy Policy)有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式AI於課程產出 Conditionally open; specify generative AI usage in course output.________________________________________與課程相關的網站 (Course-related Website)(Personal Website)https://www.nature.com/nchem/https://pubs.acs.org/https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/journal/15213773

brief:
本課程旨在培養研究生閱讀、理解及批判性分析最新分析化學文獻的能力，並訓練學生以英文進行科學簡報、回答問題及參與學術討論。學生將選
擇近期發表之高品質分析化學研究論文，整理研究背景、分析方法、主要結果及研究的重要性，並於課堂中進行口頭報告與討論。

The purpose of this seminar course is to develop essential skills for graduate research in analytical chemistry. Students will learn to 
critically read and evaluate recent scientific literature, organize scientific information, give oral presentations in English, answer 
questions, and participate actively in scientific discussions.
content: Course keywords: Analytical Chemistry, Literature Search, Scientific Presentation, Scientific Discussion, Critical Thinking      課程說明 (Course Description)本課程旨在訓練學生閱讀與分析近期分析化學文獻，並培養科學簡報、批判性思考及學術討論能力。學生將選擇近期研究論文，以英文進行口頭報告，並參與課堂問答與討論。This course aims to develop students’ skills in reading and critically evaluating recent literature in analytical chemistry, as well as scientific presentation and discussion. Students will give oral presentations in English and actively participate in class discussions.指定用書 (Text Books)無指定教科書。No designated textbook.參考書籍 (References)以近五年內發表於 SCI/SCIE 收錄期刊，且與分析化學相關之原始研究論文為主。所選論文須具有明確的分析化學內容或方法上的創新性，不接受發表於掠奪性期刊（predatory journals）之論文。所有報告文獻須經授課教師確認。Recent original research articles published within the past five years in reputable SCI/SCIE-indexed journals related to analytical chemistry. Articles published in predatory journals will not be accepted. All selected articles must be approved by the instructor.教學方式 (Teaching Methods)課程包括教師講授、文獻研讀、學生口頭報告及課堂討論。學生須閱讀並理解所選論文，以英文進行科學簡報，並回答教師及同學的問題。Lectures, literature study, student presentations, and class discussion. Students are expected to understand the selected articles, present them clearly in English, and participate actively in discussion.教學進度 (Course Schedule)Week 1 — Course Introduction課程介紹、評分方式、文獻選擇原則及報告要求。Week 2 — Literature Search and Article Selection如何搜尋、篩選及評估適合書報討論的分析化學文獻。Week 3 — How to Give a Scientific Presentation科學簡報的架構、研究背景與研究問題的介紹、結果呈現、科學論述及問答技巧。Week 4 — Effective PowerPoint for Scientific Presentations科學簡報投影片的製作，包括版面、文字、圖表、資訊呈現及常見問題。Week 5 onward — Student Presentations and Discussion學生依排定順序進行報告。每次報告後進行問答、討論及回饋。The detailed presentation schedule will be adjusted according to class size and course progress.成績考核 (Evaluation)Literature search and article selection: 15%Scientific presentation and slide quality: 30%Understanding and critical evaluation of the literature: 30%Questions and answers: 15%Class participation and discussion: 10%請假依《國立清華大學學生請假辦法》辦理。若因請假無法進行原訂報告，請事先通知授課教師，並另行安排補報告。Absence and leave will follow the NTHU Student Leave Regulations. Students who are unable to give a scheduled presentation should notify the instructor in advance and arrange a make-up presentation.AI 使用規則 (AI Usage Policy)有條件開放使用 (Conditionally open)可使用生成式 AI 協助英文文法修正、文字潤飾及簡報架構整理，但不得取代學生本人對原始論文的閱讀、理解及批判性分析。學生須自行確認所有科學內容及引用資料的正確性，並對報告內容負責。Generative AI may be used for language editing and organization of presentation materials, but it should not replace the student's own reading, understanding, and critical evaluation of the original literature. Students are responsible for the accuracy of all scientific content and references.與課程相關的網站 (Course-related Website)NTHU eeclasshttps://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw/

brief:
This course covers the fundamental theories of digital communication systems. The
focus will be on the mathematical modeling of the communication systems and the
analysis of the system performance. The core concepts are: Signal Representation;
Spectral Analysis; Optimal Receiver for Coherent and Non-Coherent systems;
Probability of Error Analysis; Introduction to Information Theory; Bandlimited
Channels; InterSymbol Interference (ISI), Equalizers, Channel Capacity,
Multicarrier OFDM.

This course discusses the theory of the fundamental limits of information transmission or processing 
and the implications of the theory for communication or data storage systems.

brief:
This course teaches the fundamentals of multi-antenna communication, which is one of the key 
technologies in future wireless communication systems. Particularly, the use of antenna array 
deliveries substantial improvements to wireless system performance in terms of data rate, number of 
connected devices, and power efficiency. This course aims to provide students with a solid 
understanding of multi-antenna communications including system modeling, channel capacity theories, 
and transceiver design.

communications, control, radar, sonar, seismology, and biomedical engineering. This course provides

content: Course keywords: 永續科技Sustainable technology, 淨零轉型Net-zero transition, 循環經濟Circular economy, 生命週期評估Life cycle assessment, 能源轉型Energy transition, 資源循環Resource recovery, 系統思維 Systems thinking, ESG與治理ESG and governance      Detailed Course Syllabus● 課程說明(Course Description)本課程以「永續挑戰—科技回應—系統評估—實務提案」為主軸，協助研究生建立永續科技的共同語言與跨域分析能力。內容兼顧全球永續議題、淨零與碳管理、能源與材料轉型、循環經濟、資源與生物質利用、ESG治理與技術實作案例，並導入系統思維、生命週期觀點與利害關係人分析。課程特別強調將工程、科學、管理與政策串接，培養學生在研究、產業與公共治理場域中界定問題、評估方案與提出可行永續技術路徑之能力。● 指定用書(Text Books)1. 無單一指定教科書；以教師自編講義、案例教材及每週指定閱讀為主。2. 選讀書目將涵蓋永續工程、循環經濟、生命週期評估、淨零轉型與ESG相關主題。● 參考書籍(References)1. Mihelcic, J. R. & Zimmerman, J. B. Environmental Engineering: Fundamentals, Sustainability, Design.2. Ashby, M. Materials and the Environment: Eco-informed Material Choice.3. Ellen MacArthur Foundation 之循環經濟報告與案例資料。4. IPCC、IEA、UN SDGs、World Bank、OECD等國際組織之公開報告。5. 課堂另搭配近期國際期刊論文與本地產業/政策案例。● 教學方式(Teaching Method)課程採講授、案例研討、文獻導讀、分組討論、課堂工作坊、學生口頭報告及期末專題等方式進行。為強化研究所層級之實作能力，學生須以小組方式針對一項真實永續議題提出技術或系統改善方案，內容需包括問題定義、現況分析、技術選項比較、潛在效益與限制、以及實施建議。● 教學進度(Syllabus)週次	單元主題	主要活動 / 作業第1週	課程導論：何謂永續科技？學程定位、學習目標與評量方式	課程說明；分組；主題探索第2週	永續發展核心架構：SDGs、行星界限、三重底線與公正轉型	指定閱讀討論 1第3週	系統思維與永續問題界定：nexus、邊界設定、利害關係人分析	個人反思短文 1第4週	氣候變遷、碳管理與淨零路徑：碳盤查、MRV、減量與移除	案例分析 1第5週	能源轉型與低碳技術：再生能源、儲能、氫能與工業減排	課堂討論第6週	循環經濟與資源循環：廢棄物資源化、工業共生、產品服務系統	分組題目確立第7週	永續材料與綠色製程：材料選擇、低碳製造、替代原料	主題摘要提交第8週	生命週期思維：LCA、TEA、環境足跡與技術比較	案例分析 2第9週	永續生物技術與生物精煉案例：食品、生質能、資源化技術	期中專題構想報告第10週	水–能源–糧食–材料 nexus 與都市/產業永續	指定閱讀討論 2第11週	數位科技與永續：AI、資料治理、智慧監測與決策支援	個人反思短文 2第12週	ESG、永續金融與政策治理：揭露、法規、企業實務	案例分析 3第13週	技術導入與擴散：商業模式、社會接受度、風險與尺度化	專題進度檢核第14週	國內外校園、城市與產業案例整合工作坊	分組工作坊第15週	期末分組專題口頭報告 I	口頭報告與同儕回饋第16週	期末分組專題口頭報告II與課程總結	繳交期末書面報告● 成績考核(Evaluation)1. 課堂參與、出席及討論表現：15%2. 個人反思短文與指定閱讀回應：15%3. 個案分析作業（3次）：20%4. 期中分組專題構想報告：15%5. 期末分組專題書面報告：20%6. 期末分組口頭報告與同儕回饋：15%本課程以專題實作、案例分析與口頭報告為主要評量方式，不另設傳統筆試；評分重點在於問題界定能力、跨域整合、資料與論證品質、技術可行性分析，以及表達與回應能力。AI 使用規則 / AI Use Policy■ 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式AI於課程產出生成式AI可用於主題發想、資料整理、語言潤飾、簡報架構設計與基礎視覺化輔助；但學生必須於作業或報告附錄中揭露使用之工具、用途與驗證方式，並對所有內容之正確性、引用與判讀負完全責任。禁止使用AI捏造數據、文獻、案例、圖表或訪談內容；未經查證直接提交AI生成內容，視同學術倫理違規。● 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website)學程網站：https://stmp.site.nthu.edu.tw/；課程資料另公告於校內教學平台。

content: Course keywords: Sustainability Governance, Systems Thinking, Circular Economy, Anthropocene, Reflexive Leadership, ESG Reporting, Just Transition, Fiduciary Duty      課程說明 Course DescriptionIn the Anthropocene, sustainability challenges are no longer peripheral to leadership— they define it. Climate change, biodiversity loss, inequality, and technological disruption are not merely technical failures but failures of governance, innovation, and leadership.This course responds to the growing recognition that effective sustainability leadership requires the ability to navigate the tension between:● Scientific and data-driven “Truth” (planetary boundaries, lifecycle analysis, carbon accounting),● Systemic and ethical “Harmony” (ecological integrity, social justice, interdependence), and● Practical “Governance” (standards, metrics, institutions, accountability).Bridging global policy and organisational practice, the course equips postgraduate students with the frameworks (ISO, ESG, SDGs), innovation strategies (Circular Economy, sustainable finance, digital tools), and leadership capacities needed to design and lead systemic sustainability interventions under real-world constraints指定用書 TextbooksKrauss, L. (2026) A climate of truth : why we need it and how to get it. Cambridge, United Kingdom ; Cambridge University Press.de Beaufort, V., Enrione, A., Winchester, D., et al. (2025) Sustainable corporate governance: advanced theories and innovations shaping the future of corporate leadership. London: GBP Publications.Charles III et al. (2026) Harmony : the King’s vision for our world. London: William Collins.McAteer, P. (2021) Sustainability is the new advantage: leadership, change, and the future of business. London: Anthem Press.McDonough, W. & Braungart, M. (2009) Cradle to cradle : remaking the way we make things. London: Vintage.參考書籍 ReferencesBoeker, E. & Grondelle, R. van (2011) Environmental physics: sustainable energy and climate change. 3rd edition. Chichester: Wiley.Sustainable Corporate Governance: Advanced Theories and Innovations Shaping the Future of Corporate Leadership (2025). London: GBP Publications.教學方式 Teaching Approach● Lectures,● Assessment of Practical frameworks● Workshops● Simulations● Roleplay● Personal Reflection● Peer Learning評分標準 GradingAssessment 1: Week 5 - "The Leverage Point” Systems Map and explanatory brief (Individual), 30%,Assessment 2: Week 12 - "The Boardroom Simulation": Governance Strategy - 2,500- word strategy document & 15 min presentation, (Group), 40%Assessment 3: Week 16 - 3 Reflexive Memos & a 1,500-word personal manifesto, & class discussion (Individual), 30%,教學進度 Course SchedulePart 1: Foundations & Systems Thinking● Week 1: The Anthropocene & Planetary Boundaries Introduction to the science of sustainability and the physical limits of the Earth system.● Week 2: Systems Thinking for Leaders Mapping interdependencies and identifying leverage points for systemic change.● Week 3: Evolution of Corporate Responsibility From CSR to ESG—analysing the historical shift in how businesses view their role in society.Part 2: Sustainability Governance● Week 4: Global Policy Landscapes Detailed analysis of the UN SDGs, the Paris Agreement and the influence of international treaties on local business operations.● Week 5: Corporate Governance & Stakeholder Capitalism The legal and fiduciary duties of directors; shifting from shareholder value to stakeholder impact.  o Assessment 1: The "Leverage Point" Systems Map (Individual)● Week 6: ISO 14001: Environmental Management Systems (EMS) An introduction to the "Plan-Do-Check-Act" (PDCA) cycle. Understanding how to implement a systematic framework to manage environmental responsibilities and improve performance.● Week 7: Reporting, Disclosure, and Transparency Navigating frameworks like GRI and TCFD to ensure data integrity and prevent greenwashing.Part 3: Leading Sustainable Change● Week 8: Values-based & Purpose-Driven Leadership Exploring the psychological and ethical frameworks required to lead in a volatile, uncertain world.● Week 9: Change Management & Organisational Culture Tools for overcoming internal resistance and embedding sustainability into the core strategy and daily operations.● Week 10: Multi-Stakeholder Collaboration Managing complex partnerships across sectors (NGOs, Government and Industry) to address collective challenges.Part 4: Innovation & Circular Models● Week 11: The Circular Economy & Regenerative Design Transitioning from linear "take-make-dispose" models to circular value chains and product-as-a service.● Week 12: Assessment 2: The Boardroom Simulation: Group strategy document and pitches.● Week 13: Sustainable Finance & Impact Investment Understanding the role of capital markets, green bonds, and ESG metrics in investment decisions.● Week 14: Technological Disruptors Techno-communitarianism and the application of AI, blockchain and green tech in tracking supply chain integrity and reducing footprints.Part 5: Ethics & The Future● Week 15: Ethics, Harmony and the Just Transition Exploring how social justice and nature’s patterns inform a holistic leadership approach to the "Just Transition."● Week 16: The "Legacy & Launch" Workshop   o Assessment 3: Reflexive Leadership Portfolio   o The Peer-Reflexive Exchange: High-energy "Speed-Mentoring" and "Shadow Inquiries" to stress-test students’ ethical boundaries and examine how personal biases impact corporate governance.   o The "Just Transition" World Café: An immersive workshop applying students’ leadership manifestos to resolve "unsolvable" micro-cases involving planetary boundaries, social justice, and supply chain integrity.   o The 2040 Simulation & Closing: A "future-back" press statement aligning manifesto principles with the Paris Agreement, followed by a final reflection on the course text—such as Charles III (2026)—that most profoundly shifted leadership mental models.Appendix 1: Example assessments1. The "Leverage Point" Systems Map (Individual - 30%)Context: Aligned with Part 1: Foundations & Systems Thinking.● The Task: Students select a specific industrial sustainability challenge (e.g., semiconductor water scarcity or global textile waste). They must produce a visual Systems Map identifying interdependencies and "leverage points" for sustainable systemic change.● Students submit a systems map accompanied by a 1,000-word explanatory brief.This tests their ability to analyse organisations and systems using advanced systems-thinking approaches.2. The Boardroom Simulation: Governance & Innovation (Group - 40%) Context: Aligned with Part 2 & 4: Governance and Innovation.● The Task: In small groups, students act as "Sustainability Steering Committees" for a multinational organisation. They are presented with a "crisis scenario" (see Table 1) involving a conflict between planetary boundaries and fiduciary duties. This requires students to navigate the tension between "Scientific Truth" and "Practical Governance".● Deliverables: 1. A Governance framework: A 2,500-word strategy document incorporating ISO 14001 principles, ESG metrics and Circular Economy transitions. 2. The "Pitch": A 15-minute live presentation defending their strategy against "greenwashing" scrutiny.3. Reflexive Leadership Portfolio (Individual - 30%)Context: Aligned with Part 3 & 5: Leadership and Ethics.● The Task: A cumulative portfolio that tracks the student’s evolution through the 16 weeks. It must include three "Reflexive Memos"responding to course insights. Students will be expected to use this in class during week 16.● The Final Entry: A 1,500-word personal manifesto on "Ethical and Reflexive Leadership" that uses the three Reflexive Memos as evidence.Table 1. Crises for Part 2 – The Boardroom SimulationSupply Chain & Planetary Boundaries1. The "Hidden" Deforestation: A major supplier in the Amazon is linked to illegal land clearing, threatening the firm's ISO 14001 certification and triggering a massive social media boycott.2. Water Scarcity Shutdown: A semiconductor plant’s primary water source is depleted due to climate change, forcing a choice between maintaining production or protecting the local community's water rights.3. The Cobalt Conundrum: A shift to EV batteries is revealed to rely on child labour in the DRC, pitting the firm's "Green Innovation" goals against human rights ethics.4. Biodiversity Litigation: Construction of a new "Green Campus" is halted because it sits on the migratory path of an endangered species, leading to a lawsuit from an environmental NGO.Governance & Reporting Scandals5. The Greenwashing Whistleblower: An internal auditor reveals that the company’s GRI and TCFD disclosures have inflated carbon sequestration figures by 40%.6. Scope 3 Shock: New EU regulations suddenly require full Scope 3 reporting, revealing that the company’s indirect emissions are ten times higher than previously disclosed to investors.7. The Fiduciary Rebellion: Shareholders sue the board for "waste of corporate assets" after the CEO commits to a Net Zero target that significantly reduces short-term dividends.8. The ESG Rating Crash: A major rating agency downgrades the firm from "A" to "CCC" overnight due to a data breach of employee personal information, causing institutional investors to divest.Innovation & Circular Economy Failures9. Circular Design Backfire: A "Product-as-a-Service" model results in high return rates and logistical emissions that exceed the footprint of the original linear model.10. The Toxic "Bio-Plastic": A new biodegradable packaging line is found to release microplastics into the soil, damaging the firm's reputation for Regenerative Design.11.AI Energy Surge: The implementation of AI for supply chain integrity causes the firm’s data centre energy consumption to skyrocket, breaching its Paris Agreement alignment.12. The "Right to Repair" Protest: A tech firm faces a backlash for software locking its devices, contradicting the Circular Economy principles taught in its own marketing.Ethical & Leadership Dilemmas13. The Just Transition Strike: Closing a coal-intensive factory to meet carbon goals leads to a total town shutdown and massive labour strikes, challenging the "Just Transition" framework.14. Political Conflict of Interest: A major political donor demands the company lobby against a new carbon tax that the Sustainability Committee has publically endorsed.15. The Hostile "Anti-ESG" Takeover: An activist investor gains a board seat with the sole intent of dismantling the sustainability department to focus on "pure profit."16. Carbon Offset Fraud: The company's massive investment in forest offsets is revealed to be "phantom credits" because the forest was destroyed by wildfire.Systemic & Institutional Disruptions17. The Regulatory "Cliff": A sudden change in government results in the immediate removal of all renewable energy subsidies, making a flagship "Green Tech" project financially unviable.18. Global Treaty Sanctions: A failure to meet new international biodiversity standards leads to the company being blacklisted from exporting to the European market.19. The Tech-Communitarian Crisis: A local community seizes the firm's decentralized micro-grid during a national energy crisis, claiming "Common Good" over corporate ownership.20. Planetary Boundary "Tipping Point": An abrupt climate event (e.g., a major permafrost melt) causes a global insurance market collapse, making it impossible to insure the firm's coastal assets.

本課程以台灣電力市場與能源戰略為主題，從電力系統物理、法制制度、市場設計、能源轉型與地緣政治風險等面向，探討台
灣在高進口依賴、孤島電網、高科技產業用電成長與淨零轉型壓力下，如何維持供電穩定並強化能源韌性。課程內容涵蓋頻率
與備轉、輔助服務、儲能與需求反應、綠電交易、LNG 與咽喉點風險、AI 與半導體用電、核能與核廢料、漁電共生、BIPV、
電價補貼及國際能源危機應變。透過案例分析與政策討論，培養學生理解電力市場作為風險治理與轉型工具的能力。
content: Course keywords: 台灣電力市場,Taiwan power market,能源安全與風險治理,Energy security and risk governance,能源轉型與電網韌性      課程大綱 (Course Syllabus)1. 課程說明 (Course Description)本課程以「台灣電力市場與能源戰略」為主題，從電力系統物理、法制制度、市場設計、能源轉型與地緣政治風險等面向，探討台灣在高進口依賴、孤島電網、高科技產業用電成長與淨零轉型壓力下，如何維持供電穩定並強化能源韌性。課程內容涵蓋頻率與備轉、輔助服務、儲能與需求反應、綠電交易、LNG 與咽喉點風險、AI 與半導體用電、核能與核廢料、漁電共生、BIPV、電價補貼及國際能源危機應變。透過案例分析、文件閱讀與課堂討論，培養學生理解電力市場作為風險治理與轉型工具的能力，並能就台灣未來電力治理提出具證據基礎的分析與建議。2. 指定用書 (Text Books)本課程不採單一教科書，以下列教材與教師每週投影片為主要指定閱讀：Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC), Energy Primer: A Handbook of Energy Market BasicsInternational Energy Agency (IEA), Electricity 2025台灣電力股份有限公司電力交易平台與系統運轉相關教材經濟部能源署與相關主管機關官方文件3. 參考書籍 (References)Paul L. brief:
Semiconductor memories have mainly two uses. One is for the calculation by exchanging data with CPU, 
MPU, etc. The other is for the mass data storage. Demands for these two applications are following; 
1. Low cost and high density, 2. High speed operation, 3. Low power consumption. Therefore, memory 
technologies have been evolved more than 30 years to satisfy these demands. Moreover, new 
application has been noticed for the calculation of AI which is called in memory computing. 
Furthermore, memory device and CPU/MPU are connected chip-to-chip and can get quite high speed and 
low power operation. I will introduce these new technologies. Following are the outline of the 
course. Part1: Basic concept of memories: 1. DRAM & SARM 2.NOR-Flash 3. NAND-Flash Part2: 1. 3D 
NAND, In-memory computing for AI calculation.

microelectronics industries.

brief:
The objective of this course is to provide students an overview of VLSI designs, particularly about 
how we manage to integrate billions of transistors to perform complex functions. This course focuses 
on three major topics: logic design, electronic design automation, and computer architecture. Students 
will learn the layered abstraction of design technology from the ground up, including 
combinational/sequential circuits, gate-level design, physical layout, micro-architecture, and 
processor cores.
